question: Members of the Legislative Council of an Indian state as nearly as may be, ____ shall be elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards and such other local authorities in the State as Parliament may by law specify.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1/3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 171** of the Constitution of India specifies the composition of the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) for states that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• As per **Article 171(3)(a)**, **1/3 of the members** of the Legislative Council are elected by electorates consisting of members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities in the state.
 
• The provision ensures representation from local self-governing bodies, which play a vital role in state governance.
 
• These members are chosen through an electoral process where representatives from various local bodies vote to elect Legislative Council members.
 
• This mechanism provides a democratic way to include local governance in the legislative process, fostering decentralized decision-making.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of Legislative Council:**

 
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house of the state legislature in states with bicameral legislatures (e.g., Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka).
 
• Its members are elected, nominated, or indirectly appointed through various processes outlined in Article 171.
 
• The Council must not exceed **one-third** of the total membership of the Legislative Assembly of the state.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• Members elected by local authorities constitute **1/3** of the total members of the Legislative Council.
 
• Other members are elected by graduates, teachers, members of the Legislative Assembly, or nominated by the Governor.
 
• The election process is conducted by the Election Commission of India under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
 
 
 
• **Role of Local Authorities:**
 
 
• Local authorities such as municipalities and district boards play a significant role in state governance.
 
• Representation from local bodies ensures that issues relevant to local administration are addressed in the state legislature.
 
• This system strengthens participatory democracy by incorporating grassroots-level governance into the legislative framework.
 
 
 
• **States with Legislative Councils:**
 
 
• Currently, only **6 states** in India have Legislative Councils: Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.
 
• States can propose the creation or abolition of Legislative Councils, but the final decision rests with Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The bicameral system in state legislatures was established to include diverse perspectives in law-making.
 
• The inclusion of local authorities in the election process reflects the significance of grassroots governance in India.
 
• It was introduced to balance representation from different sections of society and administrative units.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 171:** Defines the composition and electoral process for Legislative Councils in states with bicameral legislatures.
 
• **Representation:** Ensures inclusion of local self-governance bodies in the legislative process through elections.
 
• **Governor’s Role:** The Governor nominates 1/6th of the members of the Legislative Council, typically experts in various fields like literature, science, or social service.
 
• **Election Eligibility:** Members of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities are eligible to vote in the elections for Legislative Council members.
 
• **Relevance:** Legislative Councils provide an additional layer of checks and balances in state governance, complementing the Legislative Assembly.
